summary: In Paris, France, Paris Oasis Schoolyard Program is a monitoring and adaptive management initiative. The program used a co-design and nature-based approach Paris was able to turn heat-prone, paved schoolyards into cool, green, and accessible spaces. The project utilized community engagement strategies, climate models, and pilot projects, to successfully implement more permeable surfaces, vegetation, and water retention features to reduce urban heat and stormwater runoff within schoolyards. The case addresses extreme Heat. Available materials report dozens of schoolyards across Paris were successfully redesigned and opened to the public, Surface temperatures in OASIS yards were significantly lower compared to traditional schoolyards, Increased awareness and participation among students, teachers, and neighborhood residents, and The program is now being scaled up as a citywide adaptation measure.
title: Paris Oasis Schoolyard Program
transferability: The OASIS Schoolyard Programme is highly relevant to Washington, particularly urban areas like Seattle, which experiences increased risks from extreme heat, stormwater runoff, and inequitable access to green space. Similar to Paris, many Seattle schoolyards and public spaces are dominated by impervious surfaces that intensify urban heat islands effects while overwhelming drainage systems during heavy rain events.
